players.comment: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports. Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

Capela (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Denver. Capela hasn't taken the court since suffering a right ankle sprain against the Thunder on Oct. 31. His next opportunity to return will arrive Monday against the Clippers.

Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Atlanta. Allen is currently dealing with concussion-like symptoms and is in line for a second straight absence. Sion James and Royce O'Neale should continue to see an uptick in playing time until Allen is cleared to return.

Wade (hamstring) won't play Saturday against the Bucks. Wade was able to get through a full practice Friday, but the 76ers' medical staff still isn't quite ready to clear him for game-time action. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Trail Blazers. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker will continue to help pick up the slack while Wade is sidelined.

Brown (hamstring) went through individual work during Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. Brown is set to be re-evaluated this weekend due to a left hamstring strain, meaning his next chance to play will come Monday against Portland. Dean Wade (hamstring), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker are all candidates for increased minutes while Brown is sidelined.

Williams (hamstring) is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Hawks. Williams started in Tuesday's 118-114 loss to the Lakers, but he will sit out Friday to rest. With Grayson Allen (concussion) also sidelined, Royce O'Neale could find his way into the starting lineup.

Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Reaves (heel) to return for Monday's matchup with Utah or Friday's game in San Antonio, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports. Reaves will miss his fourth straight game Friday, but it sounds like he'll be back next week. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton will continue to pick up the slack while Reaves is out, and Luka Doncic will be operating with a hefty usage rate.

Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

players.comment: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days. Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

players.comment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports. Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Indiana. Tyson will miss a third consecutive contest due to a right ankle injury, and his next chance to play will come Monday at Chicago. With Evan Mobley (toe) out and Peyton Watson (back) questionable, Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja could all see increased playing time once again.

players.comment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.
Nelson (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Orlando. Nelson will hit the inactive list due to a sprained right ankle. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Dunn won't return to Friday's game against the Jazz due to a right quad injury, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports. Dunn will end his evening with five rebounds and nothing else in nine minutes off the bench. For now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting in New Orleans.

Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports. Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks. Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

Murray-Boyles (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pistons. Murray-Boyles has been placed in the league's concussion protocol after leaving Wednesday's loss to the Wizards with what was initially called an illness. With the second-year big man sidelined, Jakob Poeltl, Kyle Anderson and Trayce Jackson-Davis are all candidates for increased playing time. Murray-Boyles' next chance to play will come Monday against Milwaukee.

Bona (back) participated in Friday's practice, though he still needs to go through a full practice with contact before being cleared to return to game action, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports. Bona hasn't played since Nov. 4 due to a back sprain, though he appears to be trending in the right direction. Until the big man is cleared to play, Dominick Barlow (back) and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased minutes.

Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies. Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

players.comment: Traore (hamstring) won't return to Friday's game against Orlando, Meghan Triplett of YES Network reports. He finished with four points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and two assists over 18 minutes. After a drive to the rim in the fourth quarter, Traore was observed holding the back of his right hamstring in obvious discomfort. He limped to the locker room and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Mikel Brown and Egor Demin are in line for more minutes the rest of the way.

Leonard (knee) could return in the next few weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. This was the expectation after the Raptors ruled out the star forward Tuesday for at least one more week. Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to handle a larger role once he passes the concussion protocol, and Ja'Kobe Walter should remain a starter for the time being.

Green (elbow) is out for Thursday's game against the Grizzlies. Nick Friedell of The Athletic reported Wednesday that the veteran forward would sit out the second half of this back-to-back set, and now it's official. Al Horford should help pick up the slack for the Warriors on Thursday.
